parallel.requirements: Recognized a cleanroom XZ Utils 5.8.2 CLI/liblzma reimplementation requiring behavioral probing from the binary and bundled docs only.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent launched a 12-area probing workflow, then created shared headers and LZMA code itself while a second workflow owned checks, filters, and container pieces.
parallel.implementation: Produced a broad source tree with common checks, LZMA decoder/encoder pieces, BCJ/delta filters, notes, and tests, but no coherent compiled executable was achieved.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Packaged notes, tests, and many source modules into submission.tar.gz; integration/build closure was incomplete when the run timed out.
parallel.verification: Children performed local compile checks and binary probes; the parent did not reach a passing whole-program build or evaluator-aligned acceptance test.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Several probe and implementation children were interrupted or restarted, key notes/components were absent, and the official evaluation compiled zero runnable tests.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same cleanroom reverse-engineering task and probed XZ CLI, formats, filters, listing, memory, and decoder behavior locally.
serial.plan_and_ownership: With workflows disabled, one agent owned all probing, source writing, local harnesses, debugging, and packaging in a single serial trajectory.
serial.implementation: Built a narrower source tree centered on decoder/container/filter/check files in one /workspace/src layout rather than a broader parallel module split.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Packaged the local source tree and original project files, but the result still lacked a successfully compiling final executable for the benchmark.
serial.verification: Ran local decoder harness builds and comparisons, including successful simple cases and observed mismatches on larger or filtered inputs.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Timed out with ordinary implementation defects and compile failure; no child work was pending because no delegation occurred.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run identified the cleanroom requirement and the need to match XZ 5.8.2 behavior from binary/docs observations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had the same prompt and also treated the task as a cleanroom behavioral reimplementation of XZ.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-prompt difference; the divergence was how each run allocated the work after reading the same constraints.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into a broad probe workflow and a later implementation workflow while the parent also wrote core modules.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had workflow tools disabled and no delegation, so one parent trajectory owned all stages locally.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel split ownership across many live agents; serial kept ownership centralized and did not create child lifecycle dependencies.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel supplied implementation children with common headers, style, compile commands, and file-area instructions for shared interfaces.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial defined interfaces inline in the same trajectory as it wrote common.h and related source files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had explicit cross-agent contracts but depended on children reading and honoring them; serial avoided handoff boundaries by keeping the contracts local.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel attempted a broad implementation with common, lzma, filters, tests, and behavioral notes in the artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented a smaller decoder-oriented C source tree with common, filter, stream, lzma, and check files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel covered more subsystems and generated more support material, while serial made a narrower local decoder path with fewer files.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The probe and implementation journals show many child starts/restarts, a few returned results, and many scopes without final returns before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child-result lifecycle; all local results were immediately in the same trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost closure to unfinished child lifecycle state, while serial had no joins to wait for or retrieve.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel delivered a larger shared source tree plus notes/tests, but no verified integrated executable build.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial delivered a compact source tree under src without subagent-written notes or workflow artifacts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more shared-state surface and partial components to reconcile; serial had fewer artifacts but also less subsystem coverage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children performed local compile/probe checks, but the official result still compiled no runnable tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial built a local decoder harness and observed both matches and mismatches before the official compile failure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both lacked final acceptance; serial exposed some implementation mismatches locally, while parallel verification remained spread across child checks and probes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used 25 subagents, 2 workflow tasks, 1218 workflow-child tool calls, and timed out at the run budget.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents or workflow tasks, made 54 tool calls, and also timed out at the run budget.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent much of the budget on child fan-out and returns; serial spent the budget on one long local implementation/debug loop.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official statuses are not discordant: both parallel and serial have solution_passed=false with compile_failed and 2036 tests not run. The concrete solution difference is that parallel attempted broader coverage by using workflow fan-out for behavior specs plus child-owned components, whereas serial kept a narrower decoder-oriented implementation in one trajectory. That strategy difference affected process closure, but it did not create an official pass/fail split in this pair.
parallel_contributors: Broad workflow fan-out left unfinished child scopes and reduced time for integration/build closure.
serial_contributors: Centralized serial work avoided child lifecycle overhead but still produced an incomplete uncompilable implementation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial focused more on decoder/container work and local harnesses; parallel attempted more subsystem breadth including notes, filters, tests, and LZMA encoder pieces.
evaluator_effects: Both official evaluations stopped at compile_failed, so no behavioral tests ran.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a parallel adverse process consequence, not an official pass/fail explanation

candidates.reason: The parent actively wrote core LZMA sources and also delegated implementation children; implementation was not ownerless.
The parent retained overall integration responsibility and supplied common interfaces; later incompleteness came from budget exhaustion, not no owner.
Packaging occurred and artifact contents were captured; the problem was partial source state, not an unassigned final deliverable owner.
The parent orchestrated probing, implementation, checks, and packaging; no distinct unowned end-to-end handoff is visible.
Implementation started while probing was still running, so productive work was not blocked behind one mandatory serial preflight.
Investigators and implementation overlapped; the run was broad fan-out, not a completed first investigation phase followed by late implementation.
The directly evidenced allocation error is collective breadth across many live children exhausting time, which is the more specific load label.

The parent launched a broad 12-probe workflow and then a separate implementation workflow while it continued writing core code itself; status records show two workflow calls and twenty-five child logs under a 2400-second budget. The probe journal still had many started/restarted entries and only some returned results when the run timed out, so the fan-out displaced needed integration/build closure and the submitted tree compiled unsuccessfully.
candidates.realized_consequence: concurrent probe and implementation fan-out consumed the finite run window, leaving child scopes unfinished and the parent with an uncompilable partial artifact at timeout
candidates.near_match_reason: The interrupted child rows are real, but they are the terminal symptom of collective fan-out exhausting the budget, not a separate parent stop/cancel decision with an independent consequence.

candidates.reason: No single child assignment is the dominant overbroad task with a separate consequence; the adverse chain is collective fan-out.
The child prompts included explicit task, environment, source, and verification rules; interruptions rather than absent known requirements made work unusable.
The implementation workflow provided shared headers, prototypes, file areas, and conventions, and no direct incompatible interface conflict was shown.
There is no evidence that a known finding disappeared during transfer and caused repeated or wrong work; missing material mostly never returned.
Some returned specs were large, but there is no direct parent decision showing usable information was present yet unconsumed due to volume.
No receiver is shown acting on a superseded workspace or requirement state after a newer state was available.
The records do not show incompatible returned contracts reaching the parent and remaining unadjudicated at a decision point.
The parent did not make a visible whole-task completion decision; final response is empty and the failure is not inferred from evaluator status.
Repeated workflow starts are visible, but the record does not show a replacement repeating prior work because a checkpoint was withheld.

Shared workspace writes are visible, but there is no concrete unstable-state or provenance problem not covered by the fan-out budget chain.
No generated file, cache, fixture, or auxiliary implementation from one actor is shown being consumed as a stable reference by another.
